title: The Autopsy of Greywater Bay
premise: Vesper Crane, the meticulous archivist of Greywater Bay's cathedral, has spent three years cataloguing the town's grief after the drowning of local schoolteacher Maren Oduya—officially ruled an accident. When a second diary surfaces in the crypt's sealed records, written in Maren's hand and continuing for months past her death, Vesper realizes someone has been forging her voice to keep a secret buried beneath the tide. As Vesper unravels the forgery with help from the found family of misfits who orbit the cathedral—a lapsed priest, a teenage runaway, and Maren's estranged sister—they discover the crypt's lock was changed the night Maren died, implicating the town's most beloved family. In the end, Vesper must choose between preserving the archive's fragile order and exposing the truth: that Maren was silenced for what she knew about the bay's poisoned waters, and that her final diary entry names Vesper's own mentor as her killer.
about_author: August Montrose is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing coastal town archives along the Atlantic seaboard. They write mysteries where the dead speak through paperwork and small towns keep their secrets in triplicate.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Drowned Things
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. We meet the cathedral archive, its locked crypt, and Vesper's ritualized, invisible life filing Greywater Bay's sorrows. The anniversary of Maren Oduya's drowning passes unnoticed by everyone but Vesper, who still keeps her file open. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as devotion.

chapters.title: A Diary That Outlived Its Author
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. While re-cataloguing the crypt's sealed records, Vesper finds a second diary in Maren's handwriting—with entries dated four months after her death. The last visible entry reads: 'If you are reading this, I trusted the wrong person.' Emotional beat: vertigo; the ordered world cracks.

chapters.title: The Lock That Changed Hands
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper compares the crypt's lock records and discovers the key was recut the night Maren died—by someone with archive access. Only three people had it: Vesper, Father Ambrose, and the late sexton. Emotional beat: suspicion turning inward, toward home.

chapters.title: Sister of Salt
chapters.summary: Maren's sister Delphine's POV. Delphine arrives in town uninvited, having received an anonymous letter quoting Maren's posthumous diary. She confronts Vesper at the archive; their wary alliance begins. Emotional beat: two kinds of grief colliding into reluctant partnership.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Low tide exposes the old oyster beds where Maren drowned. Vesper and Delphine find a rusted strongbox wedged in the pilings containing water-damaged lab reports on the bay's contamination—reports Maren had been collecting before she died. Emotional beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Congregation of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Runaway teen Wren's POV. Wren, who sleeps in the cathedral loft, notices Vesper's obsession growing and starts secretly helping, forging archive request slips. Through Wren we see the cathedral's misfit household as a fragile found family. Emotional beat: belonging offered without being asked.

chapters.title: Entries in Another Hand
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A forensic comparison shows the posthumous diary entries are forged—but expertly, by someone who studied Maren's writing for years. The forger knew her intimately. Vesper realizes the diary was meant to be found, eventually, by someone specific. Emotional beat: the trap's shape becoming visible.

chapters.title: The Harrower Family Dinner
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. The town's beloved Harrower family—the cannery owners whose fortune rests on the bay—host their annual memorial for drowned fishermen. Delphine attends as Maren's sister and watches Edmund Harrower flinch when the tide is mentioned. Emotional beat: charm as camouflage.

chapters.title: Father Ambrose's Confession
chapters.summary: Ambrose's POV. The lapsed priest admits he recut the crypt key—not to kill, but because Maren asked him to hide something there three days before she died. He never opened it. He has been dying slowly of guilt ever since. Emotional beat: confession without absolution.

chapters.title: The Hidden Reliquary
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Following Ambrose's directions, they breach the crypt's inner wall and find Maren's hidden cache: complete contamination records proving the Harrower cannery poisoned the bay for a decade, plus a letter naming the person she feared most. The name page is missing. Emotional beat: truth within reach, torn just out of grasp.

chapters.title: Someone Is Filing Behind Me
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper discovers the archive has been searched—files subtly reordered, the forgery diary moved. Someone else knows what they've found. A threatening note appears, alphabetized correctly, in the O file. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing they are also prey.

chapters.title: Wren Runs Out of Hiding Places
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren is caught photographing Harrower cannery records and barely escapes, injured. The found family closes ranks around them in the cathedral, and Vesper, for the first time, chooses people over protocol—hiding Wren inside the crypt itself. Emotional beat: protectiveness as transformation.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Quiet Hand
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper finally examines the handwriting on the anonymous letters and the forged diary against old training documents—and recognizes the penmanship of Archivist Emeric Vale, Vesper's mentor, who taught them everything about order, discretion, and looking away. Emotional beat: betrayal at the root of identity.

chapters.title: Three Years of Looking Away
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, interwoven with flashback. Vesper reconstructs how Vale groomed them to inherit not just the archive but its silences—including the official ruling on Maren's death, which Vale himself drafted. Emotional beat: complicity confronted; invisibility revealed as a choice made for them.

chapters.title: The Storm Gauge
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Delphine finds Maren's tide logs showing she planned to meet someone at the oyster beds the night she died—at the exact hour the storm gauge recorded an anomaly. The meeting was arranged by someone Maren trusted completely. Emotional beat: the noose tightening around a familiar neck.

chapters.title: What Vale Kept
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Searching Vale's private office, Vesper finds the missing diary page and decades of hush-money ledgers: Vale has been paid by the Harrowers since before Maren died—to bury the contamination evidence and, when Maren wouldn't stop, to end it. Emotional beat: horror arriving calmly, like a filed document.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (her true final diary pages). Maren writes her last night alive: her fear, her love for Delphine, her plan to expose the Harrowers at dawn, and her plea that whoever finds this finish it. Emotional beat: intimacy with the victim; grief given a voice.

chapters.title: Low Water, High Stakes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. An unprecedented low tide will expose the oyster beds fully—for one hour. Vesper, Delphine, Wren, and Ambrose move to recover the physical evidence Maren sank there, knowing Vale and the Harrowers will come for it too. Emotional beat: the found family marching together into danger.

chapters.title: The Autopsy of Greywater Bay
chapters.summary: Climax. Vesper's POV. Confrontation on the exposed flats: Vale confesses with terrible tenderness—he killed Maren to protect the archive's 'order,' then forged her diary as a controlled confession only he could interpret. Vesper chooses chaos over order, recording everything as the tide turns. Emotional beat: the archivist weaponizing memory itself.

chapters.title: Rising Tide
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. As the water returns, Wren saves Vesper from the flats while Ambrose holds Vale until the constable arrives; Edmund Harrower's empire begins collapsing as the evidence goes public. Emotional beat: courage from the least likely hands; the family holding.

chapters.title: Recataloguing
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Weeks later: Vale imprisoned, the Harrower cannery shuttered, the bay's cleanup begun. Vesper reopens the archive to the town—no more locked crypt, no more alphabetized secrets—and files Maren's true diary under her own name, unredacted. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as honesty.

chapters.title: What Belongs to the Living
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV, closing. Delphine stays in Greywater Bay, taking Maren's old classroom. On the first day of term, Vesper, Wren, and Ambrose sit in the back row—no longer invisible, no longer alone. The tide comes in clean. Emotional beat: belonging, at last, chosen and mutual.
